annotations.text:
Three directions for the right rail, each on a different axis.

A — Two-tier ledger. Promotes the 3 things a reviewer disputes above a compact 12-stage trail. Widest scan, most information per pixel. Tradeoff: densest, and needs 300px rather than 240.

B — Working notes. The same trail written as five prose beats. Best for someone reading the answer once, cold. Tradeoff: you cannot scan it, and it does not survive a turn that failed halfway.

C — Spine + drawer. Admits that 240px cannot hold evidence at all: the rail becomes a 44px status spine, and the real inspector opens as a 620px drawer over the transcript.

Structurally the strongest — tables, plans and candidate diffs finally have room — but it costs a click, and the trail stops being ambient.

A and C compose: ship A in the rail, open C from 'How this was answered'.

Answering the second question directly: yes, what is stored is useful — but it is roughly 5% of what the pipeline already computes.

StageEvent is {stage, status, detail<=200 chars}. Four of the twelve stages emit nothing at all, and the one with the richest payload (ambiguity_gate) emits a Python dict repr that the browser detects and deliberately throws away.

Left sheet: the audit + the proposed contract. Right sheet: four stage panels drawn only from fields that are either already in QueryState or on the proposed list.

Sign out is interactive — click Sign out in the sidebar, or the dialog's buttons, to run the confirm → busy → dismissed sequence.

The other three are static. Loaders is the rule set the sign-out dialog and the login panel both draw from; Thread titles and The discussion each carry their reasoning at the foot of the artboard.
